label: Tower value separation
query: How should Tower separate value-at-stake, committed value, measuring value, and realized savings for the Kyriba program?
answer: For Kyriba, Tower needs four clearly different “ledgers,” each with its own owner, gates, and evidence. The risk right now is that Strategy/BAFO numbers blur into “savings achieved,” which will come back to bite you at Executive Decision and Value sign‑off. My take: 1) Value‑at‑stake (VAS) – strategy / thesis • What it is: The full upside if everything in LSH‑KYRIBA‑TREASURY‑2026 works across all entities and behaviors change. • Kyriba examples: max cash visibility reduction in idle balances, theoretical working capital release, fraud loss avoidance, bank fee optimization, FX P&L variance reduction. • Governance: Owned by Treasury with Tower; approved at Strategy. Not used in KPIs or comp. 2) Committed value – decision / plan • What it is: The portion of VAS you are willing to put into the business case and forecasts, with an execution haircut and timing. • Kyriba examples: “We will free $X in working capital by year 2,” “We will reduce bank fees by Y% by year 3.” Numbers live in the capital paper. • Governance: Joint Treasury–CFO ownership; locked at Executive Decision. Any scope/timeline change triggers a re‑baseline, not quiet drift. 3) Measuring value – instrumentation / methods • What it is: The rules of the game and the telemetry, not the results. Defined before go‑live. • Kyriba examples: – Exact formulas for “days liquidity on hand,” “idle cash,” “bank fee per $ of volume,” “FX gain/loss vs policy baseline.
